default_hours_legal.note: Deletion flows, export tooling, retention jobs. Same bands as above.

ts_base_salary.note: Payscale median 70,480; Glassdoor average 101,409 (small samples, self-reported).

moderator_base_salary.note: Payscale median 20.44 per hour over 2,080 hours.

moderator_seat_outsourced.label: Outsourced moderation seat, all-in

source.title: 365outsource: content moderation outsourcing rates

moderator_seat_outsourced.note: Offshore list price about 8 per hour over 2,000 hours; US BPO 15 to 25 per hour. List prices, not contracts.

mods_per_million_mau.label: Moderators per million monthly users

source.title: Snap DSA transparency report H2 2025 (human resources and AMAR files)

mods_per_million_mau.note: From DSA transparency reports: LinkedIn about 3, Pinterest at most 5, Snap about 15 per million EU users. Used when the form gives no reviewers at all.

blob_gb_month.label: Object storage

blob_gb_month.note: S3 Standard first 50 TB. Low is Backblaze B2; high is GCS multi-region.

db_gb_month.label: Database storage

db_gb_month.note: RDS PostgreSQL gp3 Multi-AZ. Low is single-AZ; high is Multi-AZ with readable standbys. Compute instances are extra and not modelled here.

egress_gb.label: Egress to the internet

source.title: Amazon CloudFront pay-as-you-go pricing: data transfer out, United States and Europe

egress_gb.note: Nobody serves media from origin. CloudFront steps from 0.085 (first 10 TB) to 0.030 (over 500 TB), 0.025 (over 1 PB) and 0.020 (over 5 PB); Bunny lists 0.01 standard and 0.005 to 0.003 on its volume tier; Cloudflare R2 egress is zero. The typical value is a large CDN at volume; the high is AWS direct to the internet for anyone still doing that.

egress_gb_per_mau_month.label: Egress per active user

source.title: Ericsson Mobility Report key figures (22 GB per smartphone per month, all apps)

egress_gb_per_mau_month.note: No platform publishes bytes served per user. The only proxy is 22 GB per smartphone per month across all apps.

db_mb_per_mau.label: Graph and profile metadata per user
db_mb_per_mau.note: Follows, profile, indexes and counters. Editable.

db_kb_per_post.label: Metadata per post or message, retained twelve months
db_kb_per_post.note: Row plus indexes, not the media. Retention of twelve months is a model constant.

compute_per_mau_year.label: Serving and feed compute per active user

source.title: Pinterest FY2025 Form 10-K: cost of revenue and MAU

compute_per_mau_year.note: Derived: Pinterest cost of revenue is 1.36 per MAU-year and Reddit 1.60 per DAU-year (both include hosting, ops staff and fees); Snap infrastructure alone is 3.40 per DAU-year. The typical value nets out storage and egress, which this model counts separately.

feed_compute_share.label: Share of that compute spent on feeds and recommendations

scale_progress_today.label: Share of the at-scale saving the network already delivers to an app integrated today
scale_progress_today.note: What an app integrated today already gets: keys, signed events, relays and follows carry most of the custodial cost and work now. User-paid providers, a media market, label and ranking providers and payment conversion are the rest. The ramp runs from here.

p2p_store_fee_remains_share.label: Share of the store commission that still applies to in-app payments once they are peer to peer on the network

source.title: CNBC: Jack Dorsey's Damus may be thwarted by Apple's strict payment rules (the precedent, not a figure)

p2p_store_fee_remains_share.note: On Nostr the app is not a party to the payment, so the store's in-app-purchase rule should not reach it. Apple has claimed otherwise: in June 2023 it told Damus that tips associated with receiving content from creators through a mechanism other than in-app purchase broke its payment guideline, and gave the app 14 days to comply (CNBC, June 2023). Precedent pending. The low case keeps the whole commission; the high case treats the precedent as settled.

scale_months.label: Months until Nostr is at scale: standards and infrastructure in place
scale_months.note: Nostr4's estimate of the time for the network to establish the standards and infrastructure that support Nostr at scale; user growth carries the rest. The ramp starts at scale_progress_today and is front-loaded: the share of the at-scale saving the network delivers in month m is p + (1 − p)(1 − (1 − m/M)²), because the standards already adopted (keys, signed events, relays, follows) carry the bulk of custodial cost (accounts, graph, storage) and deliver early, while the pieces still maturing (user-paid providers, a media market, label and ranking providers, payment conversion) are the tail. A calendar, not a stopwatch: month 1 is January of start_year for every app, and later versions of this file will shorten the time to scale as the network matures. An app's own integration time and cost are the integ_* rows, counted apart from this ramp.

integ_weeks_accounts.label: Engineering weeks to integrate signer login and the key hand-off
integ_weeks_accounts.note: Placeholder pending member figures from the research group. Person-weeks at the loaded hour; the integration runs in the order accounts, graph, storage, media, moderation, payments.

integ_weeks_graph.label: Engineering weeks to move the graph, profiles and feeds to signed events
integ_weeks_graph.note: Placeholder pending member figures from the research group. Person-weeks at the loaded hour; the integration runs in the order accounts, graph, storage, media, moderation, payments.

integ_weeks_storage.label: Engineering weeks for relay connections, outbox model and caching
integ_weeks_storage.note: Placeholder pending member figures from the research group. Person-weeks at the loaded hour; the integration runs in the order accounts, graph, storage, media, moderation, payments.

integ_weeks_media.label: Engineering weeks for user-chosen media hosting (Blossom or similar)
integ_weeks_media.note: Placeholder pending member figures from the research group. Person-weeks at the loaded hour; the integration runs in the order accounts, graph, storage, media, moderation, payments.

integ_weeks_moderation.label: Engineering weeks for labels, web of trust and a ranking provider
integ_weeks_moderation.note: Placeholder pending member figures from the research group. Person-weeks at the loaded hour; the integration runs in the order accounts, graph, storage, media, moderation, payments.

integ_weeks_payments.label: Engineering weeks to move in-app payments to peer-to-peer rails
integ_weeks_payments.note: Placeholder pending member figures from the research group. Person-weeks at the loaded hour; the integration runs in the order accounts, graph, storage, media, moderation, payments.

integ_overlap_months.label: Months both stacks run before the custodial one is retired
integ_overlap_months.note: Placeholder pending member figures from the research group. While both stacks run the app pays its Nostr costs on top of custody and saves nothing yet; migrating users in stages is not modelled, these months stand in for it.

integ_engineers.label: Engineers on the integration at once
integ_engineers.note: Sets the calendar time, not the cost: the person-weeks are divided among them. Placeholder pending member figures from the research group; low is the slower integration and the later payback.

media_sponsor_share.label: Media hosting an app still sponsors after moving to Nostr
media_sponsor_share.note: Blossom or similar: users can host their own media, apps often still pay for some of it.

cache_per_mau_year.label: A thin cache in front of relays
cache_per_mau_year.note: A thin cache in front of relays, what a Nostr app still serves itself. What the market will bear: no public price list exists, including ours, and at scale there is no vendor to lock an app in.

auth_per_mau_month.label: Authentication as a service

source.title: Google Cloud Identity Platform pricing

auth_per_mau_month.note: Identity Platform 100k to 1M tier. Low is its 10M-plus tier; high is Clerk beyond 50k.

reset_cost.label: Cost of one password reset

source.title: BleepingComputer, citing Forrester on helpdesk password resets

reset_cost.note: Self-service email or SMS plus a share of support. The 70-dollar figure often cited from Forrester is for enterprise helpdesks and is not used.

support_self_service_contact.label: Cost of a self-service support contact

source.title: Gartner, 2019 Customer Service and Support Leader poll

support_self_service_contact.note: Gartner's 2019 poll: live channels 8.01 a contact, self-service about 0.10. Read when a key hand-off is served by a help page or a redirect rather than a person.

support_live_contact.label: Cost of a live support contact

source.title: Gartner, 2019 Customer Service and Support Leader poll

support_live_contact.note: Gartner's 2019 poll: 8.01 a live contact (phone, chat, email); high is the upper end of 2025 benchmarks.

verify_price.label: Identity or age verification

source.title: Stripe Identity pricing

verify_price.note: Stripe Identity document plus selfie; Veriff 0.80 to 1.89 with monthly minimums.

verify_share_uk.label: Users needing a check per year, UK
verify_share_uk.note: Online Safety Act age assurance applies to services likely to be accessed by children. Editable.

verify_share_us.label: Users needing a check per year, US

source.title: SCOTUSblog: Supreme Court allows Texas to enforce its app store age-verification law (SB 2420)

verify_share_us.note: Most US social apps run no paid identity check today: Meta and YouTube use estimation on accounts they suspect are under age, Reddit checks documents only where a law requires it, and the Texas and Utah app-store laws put the age signal at the store rather than in the app. The share is the users an app still sends to a paid check, not the users whose age it knows.

verify_share_eu.label: Users needing a check per year, EU

verify_share_other.label: Users needing a check per year, other

verify_remains_share.label: Age checks that remain on Nostr
verify_remains_share.note: Age assurance becomes an external layer the app reads rather than buys: the Texas and Utah laws put it at the app store, the EU is building a device-level age wallet under the DSA. The UK Online Safety Act is the residual: Ofcom's duty attaches to the service a child can use, wherever sign-up happened, so a client showing others' content may still have to check. Low keeps the UK duty in full; high is the ideal.

key_handoff_live_share.label: Share of key hand-offs that reach a live support contact rather than self-service
key_handoff_live_share.note: Keys cannot be reset. A non-custodial app's support is a redirect to the user's own or a recommended key-management service; only a share of those redirects reach a person. The contact costs are Gartner's.

ranking_fee_per_mau_year.label: A ranking or discovery provider
ranking_fee_per_mau_year.note: Web-of-trust ranking or discovery as a service. What the market will bear: no public price list exists, including ours, and at scale there is no vendor to lock an app in.

graph_eng_remains_share.label: Graph engineering that remains on Nostr
graph_eng_remains_share.note: At scale, assembling feeds from relays on the client is the app's own feed logic.

gdpr_program_year.label: GDPR program for a small app (EU or UK)

source.title: Legiscope: GDPR compliance cost ranges for SMEs (vendor estimate)

gdpr_program_year.note: Vendor ranges: micro 5k to 15k EUR, small 15k to 50k. Outsourced DPO alone runs 1,500 to 8,000 per month.

uk_osa_year.label: UK Online Safety Act, small or micro service

source.title: DSIT Online Safety Act enactment impact assessment, tables 49 to 52

uk_osa_year.note: Impact assessment, 2019 prices: ongoing 6,040 GBP with moderation and risk assessment, plus 7,460 GBP transition spread over three years; low is the 87 GBP basic case; high is a small high-risk service at 50,800 GBP. Converted at 1.30 USD per GBP.

dsa_year.label: EU Digital Services Act, non-VLOP platform

source.title: ACT position paper citing the Commission's DSA notice-and-action setup cost

dsa_year.note: Point of contact, legal representative outside the EU, notice-and-action, statements of reasons. The only published figure is the Commission's 1,500 EUR setup estimate.

content_law_remains_share.label: Content-law programs that remain on Nostr
content_law_remains_share.note: The DSA's notice-and-action duties fall on hosting services, and a client that hosts nothing is a weaker target than a platform; the UK Online Safety Act still reaches a service a child can use. Low keeps three quarters of both programs, the same world as moderation's low case: the duties follow whatever the app still hosts.

us_privacy_year_small.label: US privacy program, below the CCPA threshold

us_privacy_year_large.label: US privacy program, at or above the CCPA threshold

ccpa_consumer_threshold.label: CCPA consumer threshold

source.title: California Attorney General: CCPA thresholds

ccpa_consumer_threshold.note: The law applies above 25M USD revenue, or 100k California consumers or households, or 50% of revenue from selling personal information. Compared against US users × the California share.

annual_users_per_mau.label: Annual unique users as a multiple of monthly actives
annual_users_per_mau.note: Used only to test the CCPA threshold, which counts consumers a year, not monthly actives. Access-request volume stays per monthly user.

dsar_rate_per_mau_year.label: Data subject access requests per user

source.title: DataGrail 2025 Data Privacy Trends (webinar): 1,215 requests per 5 million monthly unique visitors in 2024

dsar_rate_per_mau_year.note: DataGrail's 2024 benchmark is about 0.00024 a visitor a year; its 2023 report put it at 859 per million identities (0.00086), which is the high. Its customers are companies that bought privacy tooling, so both figures lean high for a consumer app. The 3.2 per thousand figure attributed to DLA Piper is an enterprise, manual-handling number and is not used. Applied to EU and UK users always, and to US users only at or above the CCPA threshold.

dsar_cost.label: Cost of handling one request
dsar_cost.note: Automated consumer export: a support touch plus an export job. Gartner's 1,524 a request (via DataGrail) is for an enterprise request handled by hand and is not used; the high is a quarter-hour of a privacy engineer plus review. On Nostr the requests fall with the data retained (retained_data_share), not to zero.

cyber_insurance_year.label: Cyber liability insurance, small business

source.title: Insureon: cyber liability insurance cost for small businesses

cyber_insurance_year.note: Median of policies sold. Scales with data held.

breach_prob_year.label: Probability of a breach in a year

source.title: Cyentia Institute, IRIS 2025: annualized incident probability (Figure 6, Figure A2)

breach_prob_year.note: IRIS 2025 models a 9.3% chance that a typical firm has a significant incident in a year (2024), with firms under 10M revenue at 0.60× that (5.6%) and the information sector at 8.4%. Cross-check: a small-business cyber policy at 1,552 a year and the 2025 industry loss ratio of 53% (NAIC) imply insurers expect to pay out about 820 a year per small policy, far below this row's expected loss, because the row counts the whole loss and the policy pays only part of it. Shown as risk exposure, apart from the cash costs.

breach_cost_per_user.label: Breach cost per affected user

source.title: IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report 2026: global average

breach_cost_per_user.note: IBM stopped publishing a per-record figure; earlier editions ran around 150 to 165 per record for large organisations. IRIS 2025 puts the median loss for a firm under 100M revenue at 357k. The typical value is deliberately far below the per-record figure.

breach_cost_cap.label: Breach cost cap

source.title: IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report 2026: global average

breach_cost_cap.note: The 2026 global mean. High is the US mean reported from the same edition. Expected loss is never scaled above it.

privacy_remains_share.label: Privacy program that remains on Nostr
privacy_remains_share.note: For whatever the app still retains privately.

insurance_remains_share.label: Insurance that remains on Nostr
insurance_remains_share.note: A policy sized to the data still held.

retained_data_share.label: Personal data an app still holds on Nostr
retained_data_share.note: Personal data an app still holds on Nostr: scales the expected breach loss and the access requests that remain.

ts_tooling_per_mau_year.label: Moderation tooling
ts_tooling_per_mau_year.note: Classifiers, queues, hash matching. Vendor pricing is per item and unpublished at small scale.

tooling_remains_share.label: Moderation tooling that remains on Nostr
tooling_remains_share.note: Classifiers, queues and hash matching give way to label providers and web of trust; what remains is hash matching on anything the app itself hosts.

label_provider_per_mau_year.label: A label or web-of-trust provider
label_provider_per_mau_year.note: Labels and trust scores as a service, the moderation line's Nostr-native cost. What the market will bear: no public price list exists, including ours, and at scale there is no vendor to lock an app in.

appeals_share.label: Appeals and escalation on top of review labour

moderation_remains_share.label: Moderation that remains on Nostr
moderation_remains_share.note: Review and ranking move to the network: web-of-trust weighting, interoperable algorithm configs and label events let users curate what they see, so an app that hosts nothing moderates nothing of its own. What remains is illegal-content handling for any relay or media host the app runs, and app-store filter, report and block rules. Low keeps half, the same world as the content-law low case.

apple_rate_standard.label: Apple App Store commission, standard

source.title: Apple App Store Small Business Program

apple_rate_standard.note: 30% worldwide; 26% under the EU terms effective 2026-10-01. Subscriptions drop to 15% after the first year, not modelled.

apple_rate_small.label: Apple App Store commission, Small Business Program

source.title: Apple App Store Small Business Program

google_rate_standard.label: Google Play commission above 1M USD

source.title: Google Play service fees (US, UK and EEA from 2026-06-30; other markets)

google_rate_standard.note: US, UK and EEA from 2026-06-30: 20% new installs or 25% existing, plus 5% if Play Billing is used. Other markets 30%.

google_rate_small.label: Google Play commission on the first 1M USD

source.title: Google Play service fees (US, UK and EEA from 2026-06-30; other markets)

google_rate_small.note: 10% service fee plus 5% billing fee in the US, UK and EEA; 15% elsewhere.

store_small_threshold.label: Small-business threshold for store tiers

source.title: Apple App Store Small Business Program

store_small_threshold.note: Both stores step at 1M USD a year.

processor_rate.label: Card processor rate

source.title: Stripe pricing (US)

processor_rate.note: Stripe US 2.9%; low is Stripe UK domestic cards 1.5%; high is PayPal Checkout 3.49%.

source.title: Stripe pricing (US)

reseller_rate.label: Merchant-of-record rate

source.title: Paddle pricing (merchant of record)

reseller_rate.note: Paddle and Lemon Squeezy list 5% plus a fixed fee; the reseller is the seller and carries sales tax and VAT.

source.title: Paddle pricing (merchant of record)

avg_ticket.label: Average transaction size
avg_ticket.note: Turns revenue into a transaction count for the fixed fee. A bigger ticket means fewer fees, so low is the larger ticket.

lightning_rate.label: Lightning or on-chain processor rate

source.title: OpenNode pricing and fees

lightning_rate.note: OpenNode about 1%; BTCPay Server 0%. The at-scale saving is full conversion of the app's own revenue to peer-to-peer rails (bitcoin, stablecoins); store rails are unchanged on both sides. Apple's rules still restrict bypassing in-app purchase for digital goods inside the iOS app outside the EU, Japan and the US link-out ruling, and on-ramp costs are borne by users: they affect conversion, not the app's P&L.

mt_avoidance_year.label: Legal work to stay out of money-transmitter status
mt_avoidance_year.note: Counsel and structuring for in-app balances or payouts. Charged only when the app holds user balances, credits or wallets.

mt_remains_share.label: Of that legal work, what remains on Nostr
mt_remains_share.note: An app that never holds funds has far less exposure.

growth_default.label: User growth over the next year, when not given
growth_default.note: Used only for a visitor who has not said. An app that gives no growth figure is held flat, so the projection claims nothing about its growth; the growth question on the form is the way to say otherwise.

growth_decay.label: Each year's growth rate as a share of the previous year's

source.title: Equidam: benchmarks for startup revenue growth (15,000+ ventures)

growth_decay.note: Founders' own forecasts fall from 120% to 83% to 60% a year, about 0.7 each year. A doubling app is therefore about 9 times its size in year five, not 32.

posts_default.label: Posts or messages a user a month, when neither given nor implied by the kind of app
posts_default.note: The media-feed figure, used when the form says nothing about content.

mb_default.label: Storage a user, when neither given nor implied by the kind of app
mb_default.note: The media-feed figure, used when the form says nothing about content.

kind_messaging_posts.label: Messaging app: messages a user a month
kind_messaging_posts.note: Chat is high volume and small.

kind_messaging_egress_gb.label: Messaging app: GB served a user a month
kind_messaging_egress_gb.note: Text and thumbnails. Replaces egress_gb_per_mau_month when the kind is given.

kind_messaging_compute.label: Messaging app: compute a user a year
kind_messaging_compute.note: Fan-out and presence, little ranking. Replaces compute_per_mau_year when the kind is given.

kind_feed_posts.label: Media feed: posts a user a month
kind_feed_posts.note: Most users read; a few post.

kind_feed_mb.label: Media feed: storage a user
kind_feed_mb.note: Images and short video, kept. The research puts an image-heavy feed well above the 50 MB generic default.

kind_feed_egress_gb.label: Media feed: GB served a user a month
kind_feed_egress_gb.note: The research's 1 to 5 GB a month for an image-heavy feed. Replaces egress_gb_per_mau_month when the kind is given.

kind_feed_compute.label: Media feed: compute a user a year
kind_feed_compute.note: Ranking, recommendation and transcoding. Replaces compute_per_mau_year when the kind is given.

kind_community_posts.label: Community or forum: posts a user a month

kind_community_mb.label: Community or forum: storage a user

kind_community_egress_gb.label: Community or forum: GB served a user a month
kind_community_egress_gb.note: Threads with some images. Replaces egress_gb_per_mau_month when the kind is given.

kind_community_compute.label: Community or forum: compute a user a year
kind_community_compute.note: Search and notifications more than ranking. Replaces compute_per_mau_year when the kind is given.

kind_marketplace_posts.label: Marketplace: listings and messages a user a month

kind_marketplace_egress_gb.label: Marketplace: GB served a user a month
kind_marketplace_egress_gb.note: Listing photos browsed. Replaces egress_gb_per_mau_month when the kind is given.

kind_marketplace_compute.label: Marketplace: compute a user a year
kind_marketplace_compute.note: Search, matching and payments plumbing. Replaces compute_per_mau_year when the kind is given.

team_factor_one.label: Team of one: engineering hours as a share of the default bands
team_factor_one.note: A solo founder spends a fraction of the default hours on custody work. Applied to the default hours of every area the form leaves blank.

team_factor_ten.label: Team of up to ten: engineering hours as a share of the default bands
team_factor_ten.note: The default bands were set with a small team in mind.

team_factor_fifty.label: Team of up to fifty: engineering hours as a share of the default bands

team_factor_more.label: Team of more than fifty: engineering hours as a share of the default bands
team_factor_more.note: Whole teams on accounts, content and infrastructure.

mod_heads_default.label: Reviewers, when the form names a team or a vendor but not how many

accounts_eng_remains_share.label: Accounts engineering that remains on Nostr
accounts_eng_remains_share.note: At scale a Nostr app still builds and keeps signer login, the key hand-off and session handling. Zero remaining is not defensible.

infra_eng_remains_share.label: Infrastructure engineering that remains on Nostr
infra_eng_remains_share.note: At scale, relay connection management, caching, media handling and the relay capacity the app rents still need engineering time.

jur_weight_us.label: Weight of the US among the regions chosen

source.title: DataReportal Digital 2026: the United States of America (social media user identities, October 2025)

jur_weight_us.note: The form asks which regions an app has users in, not how many in each. Each chosen region is weighted by its social media users, so an app in the US and the UK is read as 82% US. Overridable until the form asks for the split.

jur_weight_uk.label: Weight of the UK among the regions chosen

source.title: DataReportal Digital 2026: the United Kingdom (social media user identities, October 2025)

jur_weight_eu.label: Weight of the EU among the regions chosen

source.title: Eurostat: digital economy and society statistics, households and individuals (67% of those aged 16 to 74 used social networks in 2025)

jur_weight_eu.note: Derived: about 340 million EU residents aged 16 to 74 (Eurostat, 1 January 2025) at 67% is about 230 million.

jur_weight_other.label: Weight of other regions among the regions chosen
jur_weight_other.note: Set equal to the US on purpose: an app that names other regions is assumed to have as many users there as in the US, since the rest of the world is too large to weight by its size. Overridable.

ca_share_of_us_users.label: Share of US users in California

source.title: US Census Bureau QuickFacts: California and the United States, population estimates July 1, 2025

ca_share_of_us_users.note: 39.36 million of 341.8 million. The CCPA threshold counts California consumers, so it is compared against the app's US users times this share, not against total MAU.

relay_per_mau_year.label: Relay capacity rented for a user, per active user

source.title: OpenSats: Advancements in Nostr Relays (relay.tools hosting at 12,000 sats a month; strfry on a small VPS)

relay_per_mau_year.note: No operator publishes cost per user. Typical is the sourced operator figure: a thousand active users per vCPU and 2 GB, about 12 USD a month on a European VPS, which is 0.14 a user a year. Low is the same capacity with backups and monitoring; high is the strfry-efficiency claim. Applied to the share of users the app sponsors (relay_sponsored_share), rented from a provider who carries the hosting duties.

relay_sponsored_share.label: Share of users whose relay capacity the app sponsors, the rest bringing their own
relay_sponsored_share.note: Users who bring their own relay cost the app nothing. The app sponsors capacity for the rest, rented from a provider who carries the hosting duties. What that sponsorship earns as a premium or sponsored add-on is not modelled.

relay_floor_year.label: Relay capacity rented, the least an app pays

source.title: OpenSats: Advancements in Nostr Relays

relay_floor_year.note: The least an app pays however few its users: one managed relay with backups, about 50 a month. The per-user rate takes over above about 4,300 sponsored users, about 8,600 active users at the typical sponsored share.
